controls.statement: Sender domains, identities, certificates, and provider accounts are controlled.
Email authentication uses current domain-authentication practices.
Bounce, complaint, rejection, suppression, reputation, and delivery-delay signals are monitored.
Unsubscribe and preference changes work promptly and are not deceptive.
Transactional, security, operational, and marketing messages are classified correctly.
Sensitive information is not exposed unnecessarily in lock-screen content, email previews, SMS, subject lines, or push payloads.
Reset, verification, invitation, and approval messages cannot be reused or redirected improperly.
Retries do not create duplicates, message storms, harassment, or spam.
Templates handle localization, escaping, long content, rendering differences, dark mode, plain text, and accessible structure.
Provider outage, delay, duplicate delivery, and out-of-order delivery are handled.
Frequency and quiet-hour controls prevent harassment and abuse where appropriate.
Phone-number and email-address reassignment risk is considered.
Production cannot accidentally use test recipients, and testing cannot accidentally use production recipients.
Security notifications are resistant to spoofing and tell users how to verify legitimacy safely.
Search and recommendation inputs, indexes, models, and ranking rules are inventoried.
Access control is enforced before indexing, retrieval, ranking, preview, and recommendation.
Deleted, private, blocked, restricted, or expired content is removed or suppressed promptly.
Query expansion, autocomplete, spelling correction, snippets, and facets do not leak restricted information.
Ranking cannot be manipulated trivially through spam, poisoning, coordinated behavior, or hidden metadata.
Personalization uses only authorized and disclosed data.
Users can understand or control personalization where required.
Sensitive traits are not inferred or used without proper review and authorization.
Fairness, discrimination, safety, diversity, and filter-bubble risks are assessed where material.
Search and recommendation quality is evaluated across languages, user groups, cold starts, sparse data, and adversarial inputs.
Caching preserves user, tenant, audience, and permission boundaries.
Index lag, model drift, and ranking changes are monitored.
A kill switch or rollback exists for harmful ranking or recommendation changes.
Apply this checklist whenever users can communicate, publish, transact, discover other users, distribute content, install extensions, delegate capabilities, or materially affect one another.
